alert_text: JWT token validation returning 401 on all requests post-deploy. Error: invalid signature, algorithm mismatch RS256/HS256
root_cause: Dependency upgrade to jsonwebtoken v9.0 changed default signing algorithm from RS256 to HS256. All tokens signed with RS256 private key are now rejected during validation.
resolution_steps: Rollback jsonwebtoken dependency to v8.5.1 in package.json
Run npm install and redeploy auth-service
Verify token validation passing with curl against /auth/verify endpoint
Pin jsonwebtoken version in package-lock.json and document in CHANGELOG
post_mortem_summary: A minor version bump to jsonwebtoken silently changed the default signing algorithm, invalidating all active sessions for 14 minutes. Algorithm must now be explicitly declared in signing config and validated in CI before deployment.

alert_text: Postgres connection pool exhausted. Error: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections. max_connections=100 active=100
root_cause: Slow query in settlements table missing index on created_at column causing full table scans. Each scan held a connection open for 45+ seconds, exhausting the pool under normal traffic.
resolution_steps: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the slow settlement query to confirm missing index
Execute CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_settlements_created_at ON settlements(created_at)
Restart payments-api pods to clear stale connection pool
Increase pgbouncer pool_size from 20 to 35 as short-term mitigation
Add query timeout of 30s to payments-api database config
post_mortem_summary: A missing index on the settlements table caused unbounded full table scans that held connections open and exhausted the pool during a traffic spike. Index creation and connection timeout policies are now enforced via pre-deploy schema review checklist.

alert_text: Redis OOM condition reached. All write commands returning COMMAND_DENIED. Used memory: 4.00GB / 4.00GB. maxmemory-policy: noeviction
root_cause: Redis maxmemory-policy was set to noeviction after a config migration 6 weeks prior. Session keys accumulated without TTL enforcement, filling memory completely.
resolution_steps: Connect to Redis CLI and run CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
Increase maxmemory to 6gb via CONFIG SET maxmemory 6gb
Verify writes succeeding with redis-cli SET test val EX 60
Update redis.conf in Helm chart values to persist policy change across restarts
Add memory utilization alert at 75% threshold in Datadog
post_mortem_summary: A configuration migration silently set Redis eviction policy to noeviction, allowing memory to fill completely over six weeks. All Redis deployments now enforce allkeys-lru by default with memory alerts at 75% and 90% thresholds.

alert_text: SQS consumer lag spiking. Queue depth: 48,291 messages. Oldest message age: 47m. Worker throughput dropped from 1200/min to 38/min
root_cause: Worker thread pool size was hard-coded to 4 threads in application config. A Black Friday traffic spike increased message volume 30x, requiring 120+ concurrent threads to maintain SLA.
resolution_steps: Update WORKER_CONCURRENCY env var from 4 to 40 in ECS task definition
Deploy updated task definition and force new service deployment
Monitor queue depth in CloudWatch — confirm draining at expected rate
Set up auto-scaling policy on ECS service based on SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages
Add circuit breaker for downstream email provider to prevent cascade on retry storms
post_mortem_summary: Hard-coded thread pool sizing caused the notification worker to fall 48k messages behind during a traffic spike. Concurrency is now driven by an environment variable with auto-scaling tied directly to queue depth metrics.

alert_text: P99 latency on /checkout endpoint hitting 8200ms. Upstream timeout errors increasing. Error rate 23%. Normal P99 baseline: 180ms
root_cause: Downstream tax-calculation service introduced a synchronous external API call to a third-party tax provider without a timeout. Under load, this call averaged 7.8s, blocking all checkout threads.
resolution_steps: Add 2000ms timeout to tax-calc external API call in TaxService.java
Implement fallback to cached tax rates when external call times out
Deploy tax-service hotfix v2.4.1 to production
Confirm P99 returning to baseline in Grafana
Add latency SLO alert for /checkout endpoint at 500ms P99
post_mortem_summary: A missing timeout on a synchronous third-party tax API call caused checkout P99 to spike to 8.2 seconds under normal load. All external service calls now require explicit timeouts and fallback strategies as part of code review policy.

alert_text: Host disk at 100%. Container OOMKilled. Log volume /var/log/nginx: 47GB. Log rotation last successful: never. Containers restarting every 90s
root_cause: Log rotation was misconfigured after the last Helm chart upgrade. The logrotate configuration path changed from /etc/logrotate.d/nginx to /etc/logrotate.d/api-gateway but the cron job was not updated.
resolution_steps: SSH to affected host and truncate largest log files: > /var/log/nginx/access.log
Fix logrotate config path in /etc/cron.d/logrotate
Run logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/api-gateway to verify rotation works
Update Helm chart values.yaml to set correct logrotate path
Add disk utilization alert at 80% threshold
post_mortem_summary: A Helm chart upgrade silently broke the logrotate cron path, allowing nginx logs to accumulate 47GB over three weeks until the host disk filled completely. Log rotation configuration is now validated as part of the Helm upgrade checklist.

alert_text: SSL handshake failures on all HTTPS endpoints. Certificate expired 2025-10-15. cert-manager renewal job last success: 2025-07-15. Clients receiving ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID
root_cause: cert-manager ClusterIssuer was referencing a Let's Encrypt staging endpoint instead of production. Renewal attempts were succeeding against staging but issuing untrusted certificates that were silently discarded.
resolution_steps: Update ClusterIssuer spec to use letsencrypt-prod ACME server URL
Delete and recreate the Certificate resource to force immediate renewal
Monitor cert-manager logs: kubectl logs -n cert-manager deploy/cert-manager
Confirm new certificate issued and loaded by nginx ingress
Add certificate expiry monitoring alert at 30 days and 7 days in Datadog
post_mortem_summary: cert-manager was silently renewing against the Let's Encrypt staging endpoint for 90 days, issuing untrusted certificates that were discarded, until the production certificate expired. Certificate validity is now checked by an external synthetic monitor every 6 hours.

alert_text: Elasticsearch cluster status RED. 4 of 12 shards unassigned. Search queries returning 503. Node heap usage: 94%. JVM GC pauses averaging 8s
root_cause: Heap size was set to 2GB on a 16GB node, the Elasticsearch recommended 50% cap was never applied. GC pressure caused stop-the-world pauses, triggering master node to mark data nodes as failed.
resolution_steps: Update JVM heap in elasticsearch.yml: -Xms8g -Xmx8g on all data nodes
Rolling restart data nodes one at a time to apply new heap settings
Force shard reallocation: PUT /_cluster/reroute?retry_failed=true
Monitor cluster health endpoint until status returns GREEN
Add JVM heap utilization alert at 75% in Kibana
post_mortem_summary: Under-provisioned JVM heap caused cascading GC pressure that destabilized the Elasticsearch cluster and marked 4 shards unassigned. Heap sizing is now set to 50% of available node memory and validated during cluster provisioning.

alert_text: Model inference latency degraded. P50 latency: 4200ms (baseline: 120ms). Feature store cache miss rate: 98%. Redis feature cache FLUSHALL detected in audit log at 14:32 UTC
root_cause: A developer ran FLUSHALL on the production Redis instance while investigating a staging issue, mistakenly connecting to the production feature store endpoint stored in their shell history.
resolution_steps: Trigger feature store cache warm-up job: kubectl create job --from=cronjob/feature-warmup manual-warmup
Monitor cache hit rate in Grafana — expect recovery to 85%+ within 8 minutes
Rotate Redis production credentials and remove from developer .env files
Add Redis ACL rules to block FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB from non-admin connections
Enforce separate environment credentials stored in 1Password vaults
post_mortem_summary: A developer accidentally flushed the production feature store Redis instance while targeting staging, causing 98% cache miss rate and 35x latency increase on recommendation inference. Production Redis credentials are now isolated per environment with FLUSHALL blocked via ACL.

alert_text: Replication lag on read replica exceeding 4 minutes. replica_lag_seconds=247. Primary write throughput: 2400 TPS. Replica I/O thread: running. SQL thread: waiting
root_cause: A bulk inventory update job ran during peak traffic, generating 2.4GB of binary log in 3 minutes. The replica SQL thread could not apply changes fast enough due to single-threaded replication on MySQL 5.7.
resolution_steps: Set slave_parallel_workers=8 on replica to enable multi-threaded replication
Set slave_parallel_type=LOGICAL_CLOCK on replica
Restart replica SQL thread: STOP SLAVE SQL_THREAD; START SLAVE SQL_THREAD
Reschedule bulk inventory job to run during off-peak hours (02:00-04:00 UTC)
Add replica lag alert at 30 seconds in CloudWatch
post_mortem_summary: Single-threaded replication on MySQL 5.7 could not keep pace with a peak-hours bulk inventory write job, causing the read replica to fall 4 minutes behind. Multi-threaded replication is now enabled and bulk jobs are scheduled outside peak traffic windows.

alert_text: OAuth2 token endpoint returning 500. Error: connection refused to Redis 10.0.4.22:6379. Token blacklist lookups failing. Redis pod in CrashLoopBackOff
root_cause: Redis pod ran out of memory due to a missing resource limit in the Kubernetes deployment manifest. kubelet OOM-killed the container, triggering CrashLoopBackOff with exponential backoff.
resolution_steps: Immediately add memory limit to Redis deployment: resources.limits.memory: 2Gi
kubectl rollout restart deployment/redis-token-blacklist
Verify Redis responding: redis-cli -h 10.0.4.22 ping
Confirm auth-service token endpoint returning 200
Add OOMKilled alert on all stateful workloads in cluster
post_mortem_summary: A missing memory resource limit allowed the Redis token blacklist pod to consume unbounded memory until kubelet killed it, taking down OAuth2 token validation. Resource limits are now required on all stateful workload manifests enforced by OPA policy.

alert_text: Product image CDN returning 404 for 34% of image requests. S3 bucket policy updated 2h ago. CloudFront returning AccessDenied from origin. Error count: 182,441/hr
root_cause: An infrastructure engineer applied a restrictive S3 bucket policy that removed the CloudFront Origin Access Identity principal. CloudFront could no longer read objects from the S3 bucket.
resolution_steps: Re-add CloudFront OAI principal to S3 bucket policy: arn:aws:iam::cloudfront:user/CloudFront Origin Access Identity XXXXX
Invalidate CloudFront cache for /* to force fresh origin requests
Verify 200 responses on sample image URLs
Add S3 bucket policy change notification to security Slack channel
Tag S3 bucket with protected=true and add SCP to prevent OAI removal
post_mortem_summary: A manual S3 bucket policy update removed the CloudFront OAI principal, breaking image delivery for 34% of product catalog requests for 2 hours. S3 bucket policies for CDN origins are now protected via SCP and changes require peer review.

alert_text: Stripe webhook processing failures. Error: HMAC signature verification failed. Webhook endpoint returning 400. Unprocessed events accumulating in Stripe dashboard: 2,341
root_cause: Stripe webhook signing secret was rotated in Stripe dashboard by a developer testing a new integration, but the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET environment variable in ECS was not updated.
resolution_steps: Retrieve new webhook signing secret from Stripe dashboard
Update STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in AWS Secrets Manager
Trigger ECS task refresh to pick up new secret value
Verify webhook signature validation passing with test event from Stripe CLI
Replay failed webhook events from Stripe dashboard for the affected window
post_mortem_summary: A webhook signing secret rotation in Stripe was not propagated to the application environment, causing 2,341 payment events to fail validation over 90 minutes. Secret rotation runbooks now include a mandatory step to update and verify all dependent environment variables.

alert_text: SendGrid API returning 429 Too Many Requests. Email delivery rate: 0. Retry queue depth: 91,000. X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. Daily send limit reached at 11:42 UTC
root_cause: A marketing bulk email job was triggered without a send-rate limiter. It consumed the entire 100,000/day SendGrid quota in 3.5 hours, blocking all transactional emails including order confirmations.
resolution_steps: Pause marketing email campaign job immediately
Verify transactional email queue is isolated from marketing quota
Request SendGrid quota increase for marketing sub-account
Implement send-rate limiter: max 5,000 emails/hour for bulk campaigns
Separate marketing and transactional emails into different SendGrid sub-accounts
post_mortem_summary: A bulk marketing email job consumed the entire daily SendGrid quota in 3.5 hours, blocking all transactional emails until midnight UTC quota reset. Marketing and transactional email pipelines are now on separate SendGrid sub-accounts with independent quotas.

alert_text: Search index out of sync. Product count in search: 847,221. Product count in catalog DB: 1,204,883. New products added in last 72h not appearing in search results
root_cause: Kafka consumer for the product-indexing topic had been in REBALANCING state for 72 hours due to a consumer group with one dead member that was never removed. The partition assignment was stuck.
resolution_steps: Identify dead consumer: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group search-indexer
Remove dead member from consumer group and force rebalance
Verify consumer lag drops to 0 in Kafka UI
Trigger full re-index for 72-hour delta: POST /admin/reindex?since=72h
Add consumer group lag alert at >1000 messages in Prometheus
post_mortem_summary: A dead Kafka consumer member held a partition assignment for 72 hours without consuming, causing 357,662 products to be missing from search results. Consumer group health is now monitored with lag alerts and dead member cleanup runs on a 10-minute cron.

alert_text: Deadlock detected on inventory_items table. Error: Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction. Frequency: 340 deadlocks/minute. Affecting: order placement flow
root_cause: Two code paths — order placement and inventory reservation — were acquiring row locks on inventory_items in opposite order (order placement: lock by product_id then warehouse_id; reservation: warehouse_id then product_id).
resolution_steps: Standardize lock acquisition order to always lock by product_id first across both code paths
Add SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to reservation query to avoid blocking
Deploy hotfix to inventory-service and order-service simultaneously
Monitor deadlock frequency in MySQL performance_schema
Add deadlock rate alert above 10/minute
post_mortem_summary: Inconsistent lock acquisition order between two concurrent code paths caused 340 deadlocks per minute on the inventory table during peak order placement. Lock ordering is now enforced as a code review standard and tested via concurrent load scenarios in staging.

alert_text: nginx upstream keepalive connections exhausted. Error: no live upstreams while connecting to upstream. Worker connections: 1024/1024. Active connections dropping requests
root_cause: A recent nginx config change set keepalive_timeout to 300s and keepalive_requests to 10000 per upstream connection, causing connections to stay open far longer than necessary and exhausting the worker connection pool.
resolution_steps: Update nginx.conf: set keepalive_timeout 65s and keepalive_requests 100
Run nginx -t to validate config syntax
Reload nginx: nginx -s reload (no downtime)
Monitor active connections dropping below 800 in nginx status endpoint
Add nginx active connection alert at 900 connections
post_mortem_summary: An overly aggressive nginx keepalive configuration kept upstream connections open for 5 minutes, exhausting the worker connection pool under normal traffic. Keepalive parameters are now tested under load in staging before any nginx config change is promoted.

alert_text: Double-charge incident reported. Transaction IDs duplicated: TXN-8821, TXN-8822. Idempotency key collision detected. payments-api pod restarted mid-request at 09:14 UTC
root_cause: Pod restart during payment processing caused the request to be retried by the API gateway without an idempotency key. The payment processor (Stripe) received two identical charge requests and processed both.
resolution_steps: Immediately refund duplicate charges via Stripe dashboard for affected customers
Identify all transactions during pod restart window (09:12-09:16 UTC)
Enforce idempotency key generation at API gateway layer before forwarding to payments-api
Add Stripe idempotency key header to all charge requests using request UUID
Implement pre-charge deduplication check against Redis with 24h TTL
post_mortem_summary: A pod restart during an active payment request caused the API gateway to retry without an idempotency key, resulting in duplicate charges for 3 customers. Idempotency keys are now generated and enforced at the gateway layer for all payment requests.

alert_text: Rate limiter bypassed on /auth/login endpoint. Brute-force attempts detected: 48,000 requests/min from 230 IPs. Redis rate limit counter not incrementing. redis-rate-limiter pod: Pending
root_cause: The redis-rate-limiter sidecar pod was in Pending state due to a node affinity rule that required a node label that no longer existed after a node group replacement.
resolution_steps: Remove outdated node affinity rule from rate-limiter DaemonSet spec
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redis-rate-limiter
Confirm rate limiter pods Running on all nodes
Apply temporary IP blocklist for the top 10 offending IP ranges via WAF
Add pod readiness check for rate-limiter sidecar in auth-service deployment health check
post_mortem_summary: A node group replacement left the rate-limiter DaemonSet in Pending state for 4 hours before a brute-force attack revealed the gap. Node affinity rules are now tested after every infrastructure change and rate-limiter health is included in the auth-service readiness probe.

alert_text: Database migration running for 47 minutes. Table products locked. All catalog reads timing out. Migration: ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector. Row count: 4.2M
root_cause: An ALTER TABLE statement on a 4.2 million row table was run during peak hours without ALGORITHM=INPLACE or a ghost migration tool. MySQL acquired a full table lock for the duration.
resolution_steps: Kill the running migration: KILL QUERY [process_id]
Validate application still functional after lock release
Re-run migration using gh-ost (GitHub Online Schema Change) tool
Schedule gh-ost migration during low-traffic window (01:00-03:00 UTC)
Add migration review step to deployment checklist requiring gh-ost for tables >100k rows
post_mortem_summary: A full table lock migration on 4.2M rows during peak hours blocked all product catalog reads for 47 minutes. All schema changes on tables exceeding 100k rows are now required to use gh-ost and run during off-peak maintenance windows.

alert_text: Memory leak detected in recommendation-engine pods. Pod memory: 7.8GB / 8GB limit. GC overhead limit exceeded. JVM heap dump triggered. Pod count reduced from 6 to 2 due to OOMKill
root_cause: A new feature added a static in-memory HashMap to cache product embeddings. The cache had no eviction policy and no size bound, growing unbounded over 72 hours as new products were loaded.
resolution_steps: Rolling restart all recommendation-engine pods to clear heap
Replace HashMap with Caffeine cache: CacheBuilder.newBuilder().maximumSize(50000).expireAfterWrite(1, HOURS)
Deploy recommendation-engine v3.1.2 with bounded cache
Set JVM flag -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError for future diagnostics
Add heap usage alert at 80% per pod
post_mortem_summary: An unbounded in-memory cache for product embeddings grew for 72 hours without eviction, exhausting pod memory and reducing capacity from 6 to 2 pods. All in-memory caches now require explicit size bounds and eviction policies enforced via code review.

alert_text: Disk I/O saturation on RDS instance. WriteIOPS: 18,000/18,000 (100%). ReadIOPS: normal. Insert latency: 4200ms. Source: inventory_audit_log table inserts
root_cause: The inventory_audit_log table had no partitioning and had grown to 890M rows. Inserts required scanning the clustered index for constraint checks, saturating IOPS on the gp2 storage volume.
resolution_steps: Upgrade RDS storage from gp2 to gp3 and increase provisioned IOPS to 32,000
Create inventory_audit_log_partitioned with monthly RANGE partitioning
Migrate recent 3 months of data to partitioned table
Archive and truncate inventory_audit_log table
Add RDS WriteIOPS alert at 80% of provisioned limit
post_mortem_summary: An unpartitioned 890M row audit log table caused IOPS saturation by requiring full clustered index scans on every insert. The table is now range-partitioned by month and storage upgraded to gp3 with provisioned IOPS.

alert_text: Push notification delivery rate: 12% (baseline: 94%). FCM error: SENDER_ID_MISMATCH. Affected devices: iOS and Android. APNs: normal. Error started after deploy v4.2.0
root_cause: Deploy v4.2.0 introduced a new Firebase project configuration file (google-services.json) from the development Firebase project instead of production. The sender ID mismatch caused FCM to reject all delivery attempts.
resolution_steps: Rollback notification-worker to v4.1.9 immediately
Identify correct production google-services.json from Firebase console
Replace development config with production config in application resources
Add CI check to validate Firebase project ID matches FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID env var
Deploy v4.2.1 with correct configuration and verify FCM delivery rate
post_mortem_summary: A development Firebase config was accidentally bundled in the v4.2.0 production build, causing FCM sender ID mismatch and dropping push delivery to 12%. Firebase project ID validation is now enforced in CI before any notification-worker build is promoted.

alert_text: Cross-origin requests failing for mobile app. CORS preflight returning 403. Header: Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing. Affects: api.example.com requests from app.example.com. Started: 30 min ago after nginx deploy
root_cause: An nginx config template update removed the CORS headers block from the api.example.com server block while adding them to a new admin.example.com block. The template merge had a YAML anchor collision.
resolution_steps: Re-add CORS headers to api.example.com nginx server block
Run nginx -t to validate
Reload nginx: nginx -s reload
Test CORS preflight: curl -X OPTIONS https://api.example.com/v1/products -H 'Origin: https://app.example.com'
Add CORS preflight smoke test to post-deploy validation suite
post_mortem_summary: A YAML anchor collision in the nginx config template silently removed CORS headers from the production API endpoint during a routine deploy. CORS preflight validation is now included in the automated post-deploy smoke test suite.

alert_text: Autocomplete latency spike. P99: 3800ms (baseline: 45ms). Elasticsearch query: prefix query on title.keyword field across 1.2M documents. CPU on search nodes: 98%
root_cause: A product team changed the autocomplete query from a completion suggester to a wildcard prefix query on the keyword field. Wildcard prefix queries are not optimized by Elasticsearch and cause full shard scans.
resolution_steps: Revert autocomplete query to completion suggester in search-service config
Rebuild the suggest index: POST /products/_suggest/_update_by_query
Confirm P99 autocomplete latency returns below 60ms
Add query type validation in search-service to reject wildcard prefix queries on large indices
Document completion suggester as the required pattern in search API runbook
post_mortem_summary: A query type change from completion suggester to wildcard prefix caused full shard scans on every autocomplete keystroke, driving search node CPU to 98% and latency to 3.8 seconds. Query patterns for large indices are now reviewed by the search platform team before deployment.

alert_text: PCI compliance alert: plaintext card data detected in application logs. Log line: 'Processing card: 4532015112830366 exp:12/26'. Log level: DEBUG. File: payments-api.log. Incident severity: CRITICAL
root_cause: A developer added a DEBUG log statement during troubleshooting that logged the raw payment request body including card number and expiry. The log was committed to main and deployed to production.
resolution_steps: Immediately rotate all potentially exposed card data — notify affected payment processor
Remove debug log statement and deploy hotfix within 15 minutes
Truncate and rotate affected log files across all log storage systems
Notify security team and begin PCI incident response procedure
Add log scanning CI job to detect PAN patterns (regex: [0-9]{13,19}) in application output
post_mortem_summary: A debug log statement exposing raw card numbers was deployed to production and persisted in log storage for 4 hours before detection. PAN detection is now enforced in CI log output scanning and debug logging is prohibited in payment processing code paths.

alert_text: Product price discrepancy reported by users. Price for SKU-48821 showing $0.01 instead of $149.99. Affected products: 847. Source: price import job completed 22:14 UTC
root_cause: A price import CSV used a European locale (comma as decimal separator) but the import parser expected US locale (period as decimal separator). $149,99 was parsed as $14999 cents then divided by 100 incorrectly as $149.99 → $0.01 due to integer truncation.
resolution_steps: Pause price import job and disable checkout for affected SKUs
Restore correct prices from last known good snapshot (pre-22:14 UTC)
Validate restored prices against source price list
Fix CSV parser to auto-detect locale or enforce explicit locale in import config
Add price sanity check: reject any price change >50% from current value without manual approval
post_mortem_summary: A locale mismatch in the price import parser caused 847 products to be priced at $0.01 for 41 minutes. The import pipeline now enforces explicit locale configuration and rejects price changes exceeding 50% deviation without manual approval.

alert_text: Inventory count negative for 23 SKUs. sku_id: SKU-77201 quantity: -148. Race condition in concurrent reservation requests. Reservation endpoint: 12,000 req/min
root_cause: The inventory reservation endpoint checked stock count and decremented in two separate queries without a transaction or optimistic lock. Under concurrent load, multiple requests passed the stock check before any decrement was committed.
resolution_steps: Wrap stock check and decrement in a single transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
Add CHECK CONSTRAINT quantity >= 0 on inventory_items table
Deploy hotfix to inventory-service
Run corrective script to identify and zero-out negative inventory records
Notify fulfillment team of affected SKUs for manual stock reconciliation
post_mortem_summary: A missing transaction boundary around the stock check-and-decrement sequence allowed concurrent requests to oversell 23 SKUs into negative inventory. All inventory mutations now use SELECT FOR UPDATE within atomic transactions and a database-level CHECK constraint prevents negative values.

alert_text: Session fixation vulnerability triggered. Security scanner alert: session token not rotated after login. Same session ID observed pre- and post-authentication. OWASP-A2 violation
root_cause: A refactor of the login handler removed the session.regenerate() call that rotated the session ID upon successful authentication, leaving session fixation attacks possible.
resolution_steps: Add session.regenerate() call immediately after successful credential validation
Deploy auth-service hotfix
Force logout all active sessions to invalidate any potentially fixed sessions
Run OWASP ZAP scan against auth endpoints to confirm remediation
Add session regeneration check to auth service integration test suite
post_mortem_summary: A login handler refactor accidentally removed session ID rotation, creating a session fixation vulnerability that existed for 11 days before detection by security scanning. Session regeneration is now covered by an automated security test that runs on every auth-service pull request.

alert_text: GraphQL introspection enabled on production API. Security audit finding: full schema exposed. Queries: __schema, __type returning 200. Endpoint: https://api.example.com/graphql
root_cause: GraphQL introspection was intentionally disabled in the application config but a new Helm chart value GRAPHQL_INTROSPECTION defaulted to true, overriding the application-level setting.
resolution_steps: Set GRAPHQL_INTROSPECTION=false in production Helm values immediately
Deploy api-gateway with updated configuration
Verify introspection returning 400: curl -X POST https://api.example.com/graphql -d '{"query":"{__schema{types{name}}}"}'
Audit Helm chart defaults — flag any security-sensitive values that default to permissive
Add introspection check to security smoke test suite
post_mortem_summary: A new Helm chart default enabled GraphQL introspection on the production API, exposing the full schema for 6 days before a security audit detected it. Helm chart defaults for all security-sensitive parameters are now reviewed in the security checklist before promotion.

alert_text: Recommendation API returning stale results. Product last_updated: 2025-10-01. Current date: 2025-12-10. Newly launched product categories missing from all recommendations. Model last retrained: 72 days ago
root_cause: The model retraining cron job had been silently failing for 72 days due to an expired AWS credentials key used by the SageMaker training job. The job exited with code 0 (logged as success) but produced no model artifact.
resolution_steps: Rotate SageMaker IAM credentials and update in Secrets Manager
Trigger emergency model retraining: aws sagemaker create-training-job --job-name emergency-retrain
Monitor training job completion and model artifact upload to S3
Deploy updated model to recommendation endpoints
Add model artifact age alert: alert if model_last_trained > 7 days
post_mortem_summary: Expired AWS credentials caused the ML model retraining cron job to silently fail for 72 days while logging success, leaving recommendations 72 days out of date. Training job success is now validated by checking for a new model artifact in S3, not just exit code.

alert_text: SMS delivery failures. Twilio error 21211: invalid To phone number. Failure rate: 67%. Affected: international phone numbers. E.164 format validation missing. Volume: 4,200 failed messages
root_cause: A new user registration flow stored phone numbers as entered by users without normalizing to E.164 format. Numbers without country codes (+1, +44, etc.) were passed directly to Twilio, which rejected them.
resolution_steps: Add libphonenumber validation and E.164 normalization at user registration endpoint
Backfill existing invalid phone numbers using libphonenumber with user's registered country
Add Twilio error rate alert at >5% in Datadog
Deploy notification-worker with pre-send E.164 validation and dead-letter queue for invalid numbers
Notify affected users to verify phone number in account settings
post_mortem_summary: Missing E.164 phone number normalization caused 67% SMS delivery failure for international users. Phone number normalization using libphonenumber is now enforced at registration and at the point of sending.

alert_text: Full-text search returning empty results for queries with special characters. Query: 'men\'s shoes' returns 0 results. Expected: 4,821. Error: Elasticsearch query_string parse exception: failed to parse query
root_cause: User input was being passed directly to Elasticsearch query_string query without escaping special characters. Apostrophes and other Lucene special characters caused query parse failures.
resolution_steps: Switch from query_string to match query type for user-facing search input
Add input sanitization: escape Lucene special chars [+ - = && || > < ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \ /]
Deploy search-service fix
Test with sample special character queries: apostrophes, ampersands, quotes
Add special character search test cases to regression suite
post_mortem_summary: Unescaped user input passed to Elasticsearch query_string caused parse failures for any search query containing Lucene special characters. User-facing search now uses the match query type which handles special characters safely without manual escaping.

alert_text: LDAP authentication failing for enterprise SSO users. Error: LDAP bind failed: InvalidCredentialsError. Affects: 23 enterprise accounts. Active Directory domain controller unreachable from auth-service pod
root_cause: A network security group rule update blocked outbound port 636 (LDAPS) from the Kubernetes node group CIDR to the Active Directory domain controller IP range. The rule was part of a broad security hardening sweep.
resolution_steps: Add NSG rule allowing outbound TCP 636 from K8s node CIDR to AD domain controller IP range
Verify LDAP connectivity: ldapsearch -H ldaps://ad.internal -D 'svc_auth@corp.example.com'
Confirm SSO login working for affected enterprise accounts
Document AD connectivity requirements in network runbook
Add LDAP connectivity synthetic monitor to catch future breaks proactively
post_mortem_summary: A security hardening NSG rule blocked LDAPS outbound traffic, breaking enterprise SSO for 23 accounts for 40 minutes. Network change reviews now include validation against a documented service connectivity matrix to prevent unintended port blocks.

alert_text: Currency conversion returning incorrect amounts. EUR to USD rate: 1.0 (hardcoded). Expected rate: 1.087. Revenue impact: -$8.70 per €100 transaction. Affects all EUR transactions since 08:00 UTC
root_cause: The daily exchange rate refresh job failed silently at 08:00 UTC when the exchange rate API responded with a 503. The fallback behavior returned a default rate of 1.0 instead of the last cached valid rate.
resolution_steps: Immediately update exchange rate cache with correct EUR/USD rate from backup provider
Patch fallback logic to use last valid cached rate, not 1.0, when refresh fails
Calculate revenue impact for EUR transactions since 08:00 UTC and issue corrections
Add secondary exchange rate API provider as fallback
Add exchange rate staleness alert if cache not refreshed within 2 hours
post_mortem_summary: A failed exchange rate refresh fell back to a hardcoded 1.0 rate instead of the last valid cached value, undercharging EUR transactions by 8.7% for 33 minutes. The fallback now uses the last successful cache value with a secondary provider if the primary fails.

alert_text: Elasticsearch data node disk at 93%. Watermark threshold reached. Shard allocation disabled: cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.high=90%. All index writes returning 429 FORBIDDEN
root_cause: The product review index was not configured with ILM (Index Lifecycle Management) and was growing indefinitely. 14 months of raw review data (67GB) was stored with no rollover or deletion policy.
resolution_steps: Add ILM policy to product-reviews index: hot phase 7 days, warm 30 days, delete after 90 days
Manually delete indices older than 90 days: DELETE /product-reviews-2024-09-*
Confirm disk usage drops below 85% watermark
Enable shard allocation: PUT /_cluster/settings {"transient":{"cluster.routing.allocation.enable":"all"}}
Apply ILM policies to all indices in Elasticsearch cluster
post_mortem_summary: A review index with no ILM policy accumulated 67GB of data over 14 months until disk watermark thresholds disabled all shard allocation. ILM policies are now mandatory for all Elasticsearch indices and audited monthly.

alert_text: RDS automated backup failing for 19 consecutive days. Error: DB instance storage is full. Cannot write WAL segments for backup. Free storage: 0 bytes / 100GB
root_cause: A combination of table bloat from unvacuumed PostgreSQL tables and un-compressed WAL archiving filled the 100GB RDS instance storage. The storage auto-scaling threshold was set too high (80GB) relative to the alert threshold.
resolution_steps: Immediately modify RDS instance to add 200GB storage (online operation)
Run VACUUM FULL on bloated tables: pg_catalog_bloat query to identify top candidates
Enable WAL compression: SET wal_compression = on in RDS parameter group
Lower storage auto-scale threshold to 60% utilization
Restore automated backups and verify snapshot creation
post_mortem_summary: Table bloat and uncompressed WAL archiving filled RDS storage over 19 days, silently disabling automated backups. Regular VACUUM scheduling, WAL compression, and storage utilization alerting are now in place to prevent silent backup failures.

alert_text: API versioning conflict. /v1/products and /v2/products returning identical responses after deploy. Version routing regex in nginx: ^/v[0-9]+ not matching correctly. v2 handler never invoked
root_cause: The nginx location block for /v2 was placed after a catch-all /v1 location block. Nginx uses first-match routing for location blocks, so all versioned requests were routed to /v1.
resolution_steps: Reorder nginx location blocks: specific version blocks before catch-all
Test routing: curl https://api.example.com/v2/products/1 returns v2 schema
Add version header validation: X-API-Version must match URL path version
Reload nginx: nginx -s reload
Add routing smoke tests for all API versions to post-deploy suite
post_mortem_summary: Incorrect nginx location block ordering caused all /v2 API traffic to be silently routed to /v1 handlers after a config change. Version routing is now validated by automated smoke tests that verify distinct responses for each API version.

alert_text: Product variants API timeout. Endpoint: GET /products/:id/variants. Response time: 28s. Query executing: SELECT * FROM product_variants JOIN product_attributes JOIN attribute_values WHERE product_id = ? (N+1 query pattern detected)
root_cause: A recent refactor introduced an N+1 query pattern in the product variants endpoint. For each variant, the ORM was executing a separate query for attributes and another for attribute values, resulting in 47 queries for a single product with 15 variants.
resolution_steps: Add eager loading for product_attributes and attribute_values in ORM query
Use JOIN query with explicit SELECT to retrieve all variant data in 1 query
Add query count assertion in test: assert db.query_count < 3 for variants endpoint
Implement response cache for product variants with 60s TTL
Add slow query alert for any endpoint exceeding 500ms P95
post_mortem_summary: An ORM refactor introduced an N+1 query pattern that executed 47 database queries for a single product variant request, causing 28 second response times. Eager loading is now enforced and query count assertions are included in the endpoint test suite.

alert_text: MFA enrollment emails not being sent. New user registrations: 1,842 users with MFA pending. Email delivery: 0. SES sending quota remaining: 50,000. auth-service logs: SMTP connection timeout to email-service:587
root_cause: The internal email-service had been scaled to 0 replicas by an accidental kubectl scale command run in production instead of staging. The command was in a developer's terminal history from a staging optimization.
resolution_steps: kubectl scale deployment/email-service --replicas=3 -n production
Verify SMTP connectivity from auth-service
Trigger retry for all pending MFA enrollment emails in the queue
Implement accidental scale protection: add minReplicas=1 to HPA for critical services
Audit kubectl context management — enforce kubie or kubectx prompt display in terminal
post_mortem_summary: An accidental kubectl scale command in the wrong context scaled the email service to 0 replicas in production, blocking MFA enrollment for 1,842 new users. Critical services now have HPA minReplicas=1 enforced and kubectl context is displayed prominently in terminal prompts.

alert_text: 3DS authentication bypass detected. Payments processing without 3DS challenge for cards requiring SCA (Strong Customer Authentication). Regulatory non-compliance: PSD2. Estimated affected volume: 2,100 transactions
root_cause: A feature flag REQUIRE_3DS was set to false in the production feature flag service during a testing window and was never re-enabled. The flag had no expiry and was not included in the deployment checklist review.
resolution_steps: Immediately set REQUIRE_3DS=true in feature flag service
Audit all transactions during bypass window for SCA compliance
Submit regulatory report to payment processor for affected transactions
Add feature flag expiry enforcement: flags without expiry dates are blocked in production
Add 3DS bypass detection to payment monitoring: alert if 3DS skipped for SCA-required cards
post_mortem_summary: A testing feature flag disabling 3DS authentication was never re-enabled, allowing 2,100 transactions to bypass Strong Customer Authentication in violation of PSD2. Feature flags in production now require expiry dates and compliance-impacting flags are monitored continuously.

alert_text: Notification deduplication failure. Users receiving 47 copies of order confirmation email. Order ID: ORD-88221. SQS message redelivery: visibility timeout set to 1s (should be 300s). Message processed 47 times
root_cause: The SQS message visibility timeout was inadvertently set to 1 second during a parameter store update. Processing took 8 seconds, causing messages to become visible again before completion and be processed multiple times.
resolution_steps: Update SQS visibility timeout to 300 seconds via AWS console
Purge affected messages from DLQ to prevent further reprocessing
Implement idempotency check using message deduplication ID before sending
Add SQS visibility timeout validation to infrastructure deployment checklist
Apologize to affected customers and provide discount code
post_mortem_summary: A 1-second SQS visibility timeout caused order confirmation emails to be sent 47 times to affected customers as messages were reprocessed faster than they could complete. Idempotency checks are now enforced before every notification send and visibility timeout changes require infrastructure review.

alert_text: Search relevance degraded. Click-through rate dropped 31% after deploy v5.1.0. BM25 scoring weights changed. top-result relevance score: 0.21 (was 0.87). Boost multiplier: 0.1 (was 10.0)
root_cause: A config file decimal point typo changed the title field boost multiplier from 10.0 to 0.1, causing title matches to be weighted 100x less than intended. The change was in a JSON config file and was not caught by CI.
resolution_steps: Rollback search-service to v5.0.9 immediately
Identify typo in elasticsearch_config.json: title.boost: 0.1 → 10.0
Add config validation test: assert boost values within expected range [1.0, 20.0]
Deploy v5.1.1 with fix and config validation
Monitor CTR and relevance metrics for 24h post-deploy
post_mortem_summary: A decimal point typo reduced the search title boost multiplier from 10.0 to 0.1, degrading search relevance and dropping click-through rate by 31% within hours of deployment. Numeric config values for search parameters are now validated against expected ranges in CI.

alert_text: Scheduled job failed: nightly_inventory_reconciliation. Exit code: 137 (OOMKilled). Kubernetes job resource limit: memory=256Mi. Dataset size: 2.1M records. Job not completed for 3 consecutive nights
root_cause: The nightly reconciliation job dataset grew from 200k to 2.1M records over 6 months but the Kubernetes job memory limit was never updated. The job was OOMKilled at the same point each night without alerting.
resolution_steps: Increase job memory limit from 256Mi to 2Gi in job manifest
Add streaming/batching to reconciliation logic: process in 50k record chunks
Trigger manual reconciliation run to catch 3-night gap
Set up Kubernetes job failure alerting via Prometheus job_failed metric
Add memory profiling step to job performance review checklist
post_mortem_summary: A Kubernetes batch job was silently OOMKilled every night for 3 days because memory limits were never updated as the dataset grew 10x. All Kubernetes jobs now have failure alerts and memory limits are reviewed quarterly as part of capacity planning.

alert_text: API response compression causing corruption. Gzip response body corrupt for requests with Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br. Error: incorrect data check. Affects: all JSON responses >1KB. Started after nginx upgrade 1.24.0→1.25.2
root_cause: nginx 1.25.2 changed the default gzip_proxied setting behavior when upstream servers send Transfer-Encoding: chunked. The double-compression from both upstream and nginx was corrupting response bodies.
resolution_steps: Set gzip_proxied off in nginx.conf to disable nginx-level compression when upstream handles it
Verify response integrity: curl --compressed https://api.example.com/products | python -m json.tool
Reload nginx
Add Content-Encoding validation to API response integration tests
Pin nginx version to 1.24.0 until 1.25.2 behavior is fully understood
post_mortem_summary: An nginx version upgrade changed double-compression behavior, corrupting all JSON responses larger than 1KB for clients supporting gzip. Response compression is now validated in integration tests and nginx upgrades require explicit compression behavior testing.

alert_text: Category tree returning infinite loop. GET /categories returning 200 but body: [object Object][object Object]... Response size: 847MB. Server CPU: 100%. Category parent_id circular reference detected: CAT-441 → CAT-228 → CAT-441
root_cause: A data migration script incorrectly set parent_id on two categories to create a circular reference. The API serializer had no cycle detection and serialized infinitely until memory was exhausted.
resolution_steps: Immediately add depth limit of 10 to category tree serializer as emergency fix
Fix circular reference in database: UPDATE categories SET parent_id=NULL WHERE id='CAT-441'
Add database constraint: CHECK that parent_id does not create cycles (via recursive CTE validation)
Add cycle detection to category tree builder using visited node set
Deploy fix and verify /categories response size reasonable (<50KB)
post_mortem_summary: A data migration created a circular parent_id reference in the category hierarchy, causing the tree serializer to loop infinitely and return 847MB responses that saturated CPU. Cycle detection is now enforced in the serializer and a database constraint prevents circular references.

alert_text: Refresh token rotation not working. Users logged out unexpectedly after 15 minutes. Error: refresh_token_already_used. Token reuse detection falsely triggering. Redis cluster in split-brain state
root_cause: A Redis Cluster failover caused a brief split-brain condition where two nodes both accepted writes for the same key slot. Refresh tokens written during this window were persisted on the minority partition and lost after cluster recovery.
resolution_steps: Resolve Redis Cluster split-brain: identify majority partition and force minority to rejoin
Implement grace period for refresh token reuse: allow same token once within 5s window
Add Redis Cluster health check to auth-service startup probe
Switch refresh token storage to use WAIT 1 0 command to ensure replica acknowledgment
Add split-brain detection alert on Redis Cluster node count
post_mortem_summary: A Redis Cluster split-brain condition during failover caused refresh tokens to be lost from the minority partition, triggering false reuse detection and logging out users. Refresh token writes now use WAIT for replica confirmation and a grace period handles clock skew during failover.

alert_text: Recurring subscription charge failures. Error: Card expired for 4,821 subscriptions. Dunning management not triggered. Subscription renewal job ran successfully but charged 0 subscriptions. Dry-run flag: true
root_cause: The subscription renewal cron job had a DRY_RUN=true environment variable set for testing that was never removed. The job logged successful execution and sent no actual charges for 3 billing cycles.
resolution_steps: Set DRY_RUN=false in subscription-service ECS task definition
Run immediate retry for all subscriptions that missed the last 3 billing cycles
Implement dunning emails for failed/missed charges
Add charge count assertion: alert if renewal job processes 0 charges on expected billing date
Audit all cron jobs for leftover testing environment variables
post_mortem_summary: A DRY_RUN=true flag left from testing prevented 4,821 subscription charges across 3 billing cycles. All scheduled financial jobs now include a post-execution charge count validation and dry-run flags require explicit removal tickets before production deployment.

alert_text: A/B test personalization serving wrong variant. Variant B (new model) should be 10% traffic. Actual Variant B traffic: 100%. Feature flag rollout misconfigured. All users receiving experimental recommendations
root_cause: The A/B test was configured with rollout percentage as a string '10' instead of integer 10 in the LaunchDarkly flag configuration. The SDK treated non-integer percentage as 100% rollout.
resolution_steps: Update LaunchDarkly flag rollout from string '10' to integer 10 immediately
Verify traffic split in LaunchDarkly dashboard shows 90/10 distribution
Analyze recommendation performance data from the 100% rollout window for insights
Add type validation to feature flag configuration deployment script
Document LaunchDarkly rollout percentage type requirement in A/B testing runbook
post_mortem_summary: A string-typed rollout percentage in LaunchDarkly caused the SDK to interpret it as 100% rollout instead of 10%, exposing all users to an experimental recommendation model. Feature flag configurations now include type validation in the deployment pipeline.

alert_text: Point-in-time recovery test failed. RTO exceeded: recovery took 6.5 hours, SLA requires 2 hours. pg_basebackup restore succeeded but WAL replay stalled at 40%. WAL files missing from S3 archive for window 14:00-18:00 UTC on 2025-10-03
root_cause: The WAL archiving script had an intermittent S3 upload failure for a 4-hour window on 2025-10-03 due to S3 throttling. The failure was logged but no alert was fired, leaving a 4-hour gap in the WAL archive that only surfaced during a recovery test.
resolution_steps: Implement WAL archive completeness check: verify no gaps in sequence numbers every 15 minutes
Add S3 upload retry with exponential backoff to WAL archive script
Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration for WAL uploads to reduce throttling
Add alert: fire PagerDuty if WAL archive gap exceeds 5 minutes
Schedule monthly PITR recovery drills and track actual RTO against SLA
post_mortem_summary: Silent WAL archiving failures left a 4-hour gap in the database recovery archive that was only discovered during a PITR drill, causing RTO to exceed SLA by 4.5 hours. WAL archive completeness is now continuously validated and gaps trigger immediate PagerDuty alerts.
